Provenance-verification slice: compiled skill facts/rules B-01 through B-31 of .claude/skills/bookminder/ (ids in use: B-01..B-10, B-20..B-31; B-32 is a post-compile author-directed addition with no mining provenance — skip it). Repo /home/user/BookMinder, branch claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s. Format+method reference (follow its verdict-table format exactly): .coordination/compile/provenance-verification-P12-P14.md.

For each rule in your range:
1. Resolve and read sources: `source .venv/bin/activate; python3 .coordination/tools/rule.py -r B-NN -c 60` from repo root — prints raw corpus fragments plus numbered transcript windows around every cited day-NNN:LNNN loc. Watch stderr for unresolved ids. A corpus id may exist in BOTH .coordination/mining/v2/ and .coordination/mining/pairing/ as DISTINCT entries — verify each separately. Non-corpus sources (ledger L-NN, threads.md rulings, verified@tree stamps, CLAUDE.md lines) are OUT OF SCOPE — mark them so; tree-verification was a separate pass.
2. Judge each corpus source against its transcript window, never against the YAML summary alone: QUOTE (character-exact at cited loc), EPISODE (does because/what-happened match the actual exchange; distortion subtypes seen so far: embellished-because, misattribution), GENERALIZATION (does the rule follow from the episode, or overreach — episode-specific instruction universalized — or dropped-qualifier), MISSED CONTEXT (material shortly before/after that changes the lesson, e.g. a later reversal). Verdict per source: FAITHFUL | DISTORTED(subtype) | OVERREACH(how) | UNDERREACH(what missed).
3. Per-rule ROLL-UP: does the compiled wording capture what its scenarios actually taught? Where it does not, propose a concrete rewording / split / standalone rule, grounded in the windows you read (cite day:loc). Do NOT edit the skill — a downstream judge applies changes.

DELIVERABLE: .coordination/compile/provenance-verification-bookminder-1.md — verdict table (rule | source | quote | episode | generalization | missed-context | verdict), short notes only for non-FAITHFUL rows, then roll-ups ONLY for rules where you propose a change. Never hard-wrap prose (one line per bullet/paragraph; tables exempt). No praise, no meta-narration. Commit ONLY that file, push -u origin claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s (retry 4x, backoff 2/4/8/16s, network errors only).

RETURN (max 10 lines): verdict counts, non-FAITHFUL ids with one-word reasons, count of rules with change proposals, commit SHA.

33	## Notes on non-FAITHFUL entries
34	
35	**p003-R7 — UNDERREACH.** The mined rule stops at "which durable home does X get: a CLAUDE.md rule or a toolchain setting". The window shows the agent answering that question three times over in one turn: one CLAUDE.md line (L1808-L1814, which survived), a new 124-line `docs/pre-commit-workflow.md` (L1818-L1828), and a `fix-and-stage.sh` helper script (L1831-L1842). The author rejected the chmod (L1847) and criticized the doc as "something that you wanted to tell me in Claude Code console output" (L1850). The episode therefore carries a second, tighter lesson the entry drops: the durable home is the smallest existing one, and manufacturing a new document or script to hold a one-line lesson is the same evaporation failure wearing a diff. Any P-14 revision that leans on p003-R7 should carry that qualifier, or it will license exactly the artifact-inflation this episode ended in.
36	
37	**p013-R7 — DISTORTED.** The `because` reads "The author explicitly demanded comprehension, not compliance, before letting the rule be written into the constitution." Nothing in the window concerns writing to CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md; the demand at L1597-L1603 gates a *commit*, and the agent's reply is a three-point explanation, not a rules-file diff. The distortion inflates the episode into a constitution-amendment gate it never was. The episode's actual force is the opposite direction and stronger: at L1647-L1650 the author corrected the reasoning the agent had restated — the emoji was to be kept, and the dual Pro/Flash attribution was a specific historical credit from day-011, not a general standard. Two of three restated reasons were wrong, and the restatement is what made that visible. `because_source: user-verbatim` overstates: the quote is verbatim, the `because` is not.
38	
39	**p021-R8 v2 — DISTORTED.** The `because` claims "the author enumerated all of them" for the list-recent story, the filter story, the implementation and two doc sections. He did not. At L7068-L7070 he names the time-control problem and then issues a general directive to "review our stories, scenatios and implementations for consistency". The enumeration appears at L7181-L7184 in the agent's own TodoWrite, after the fact. What the author did do — twice — is catch specific stale text the agent had left behind (L7113, L7124). The rule survives the correction, but its evidentiary weight is "the agent's sweep was incomplete twice and the author caught it", not "the author supplied the invalidation list".
40	
41	## Roll-up (a) — P-12 and the pending revision
42	
43	P-12 as compiled reads: *Account for everything in the tree. When a file appears that no requirement produced, surface it yourself before the partner finds it; when asked to change something, change it in place — never a parallel copy alongside the original.* All four sources verify clean at the episode level, and two of them (p018-R9, p021-R2) map directly onto the second clause; the parallel-copy prohibition is the best-evidenced sentence in the rule, attested in two independent sessions with two different failure shapes — a rejected `*_improved` file and a committed `*_v2` spec.
44	
45	The **census trigger** is supported in substance but not in the periodic form. The author never asked for a periodic sweep; he ran five audits himself, and the mined "periodically census" is agent-synthesized mechanism sitting under a `because_source: user-verbatim` label. What the transcripts do show is that every audit follows a structural event: an editable install producing `bookminder.egg-info` (day-002:L1842), a bulk directory cleanup (L1131), a tooling/pre-commit batch (L2792), and — in day-021 — a parallel spec file that survived a commit before being caught (L1288). The evidence supports an event-triggered census (after any install, scaffold, tooling change, or before a commit), not a cadence. A revision that writes "periodically" imports a mechanism no episode attests; a revision that names the triggering events is fully carried by the corpus.
46	
47	The **rejected-edit clause** is supported and overdue. p004-R11 is currently listed as a merged source for P-12 while none of its content appears in the compiled sentence — the rule as written has nothing to say about a diff that was proposed and refused. The episode verifies exactly: the author could not tell whether the hatchling change had reached disk and had to ask (day-004:L487), and needed a second turn (L494) to learn that rejected diffs are never written. The clause belongs in P-12 because it is the same obligation — the state of the tree is yours to account for, including the parts of it you did *not* change. Two precisions from the transcript: the agent's answer was correct, so the clause is about volunteering file state unprompted rather than about correcting an error; and the entry is classed `reciprocal` in the corpus while P-12 is a mirror rule, which is defensible here (it is a claim about your own tree, not a check on the partner) but should be a deliberate call, not an accident of merging.
48	
49	Verdict on the revision: the full verified evidence supports both additions, with one correction — drop "periodically" in favour of the structural triggers the episodes actually share.
50	
51	## Roll-up (b) — P-14 and the over-merge question
52	
53	P-14 as compiled carries three clauses: second-correction to durable repair in the same turn; retract every copy and correct the record; revert a wrong rule rather than patching around it. Fourteen entries are merged into it, but they are not fourteen independent episodes — p006-R3 and d006-R15 are the same author turn at day-006:L2511 split across two corpus files, so the apparent support for the retraction clause is one episode, not two. Clause coverage is otherwise real: p002-R4 and p003-R7 and p011-R11 carry clause 1, p006-R3/d006-R15 and p014-R5 and p021-R8-v2 carry clause 2, p002-R7 carries clause 3, and p005-R5 is the source of the "your future carefulness is not a mechanism" because.
54	
55	On the four entries under question:
56	
57	**p013-R7 — deserves standalone expression.** Nothing in P-14 asks you to restate the reasoning behind a correction in your own words, and nothing invites the partner to correct the reasoning rather than the output. The episode shows why the move earns its own rule: the restatement was wrong on two of three points and the author caught it *because* the reasoning was on the table (day-013:L1647-L1650). By P-14's own logic — a rule that ends as advice evaporates — a rule written down but misunderstood is not a mechanism either, so this is a complement to P-14, not a sub-case of it. It is a mirror move.
58	
59	**p018-R3 — deserves standalone expression, or P-14's verb must change.** P-14 says "propose the durable repair". The episode is the failure of proposing: "Noted." at day-018:L1243, then "Should I add this rule to CLAUDE.md?" at L1269, with three author prompts before the rule reached even a todo item. The specifics the merge dropped — write it in the same turn, name the file and section, never answer "Noted." — are the observable part; "propose" is not falsifiable in the same way. The same failure recurs at day-002:L1228 and day-021:L1722 ("Please remember that", never written), so this is a three-session pattern, not one incident. Strengthening P-14's clause 1 from "propose" to "write, and name the file and section" would carry it; a standalone rule would carry it more visibly.
60	
61	**p021-R8 — the question rests on a mis-identified entry.** "Commit inferior-then-improved" is `pairing/day-021.yaml` p021-R8 @ day-021:L1722, dispositioned to P-26, and P-26 does express it ("consider committing the inferior version first so the diff between the two carries the reasoning"). It is not in P-14 and was not over-merged there. The entry that *is* merged into P-14 is `v2/day-021.yaml` p021-R8 @ day-021:L7069, whose lesson is a consistency sweep after new evidence invalidates prior claims. P-14's clause 2 is framed around retracting *a claim*; this episode is wider — one discovery invalidated stories, scenarios, an implementation and two doc sections at once. That is an underreach of a word, not a missing rule: clause 2 should read as sweeping every artifact that repeats an invalidated claim, whether the trigger was your retraction or new evidence.
62	
63	**p003-R13 — deserves standalone expression, and not in mirror.md.** It is dispositioned to P-28 with "(part)" credited to P-14, but neither compiled text expresses it. P-28 is "Teach when asked why"; P-14 is about your own repeated corrections. Nothing in either says: when the partner names a process failure of his own, extract the mechanism, and do not console him or reframe the loss as an investment. The evidence is unusually clean — the author's self-assessment at day-003:L2305 and the agent's verbatim "Consider it an investment rather than procrastination!" at L2320 — and the move is reciprocal, about how you receive the partner's self-criticism, so it belongs in reciprocal.md rather than as a P-14 clause.
64	
65	One entry outside the question deserves the same scrutiny: **p002-R10** (apply a named principle to every instance it covers; report the full sweep, day-002:L1096) verifies clean and is likewise absent from P-14's text. It, p021-R8-v2, and p006-R3/d006-R15 are three shapes of one sweep obligation — sweep after a correction, sweep after new evidence, sweep after a retraction — which suggests the clean revision is a single explicit sweep clause in P-14 rather than three implicit ones.
66	
67	Provenance flags carried by this pass, none of which change a verdict: `because_source: user-verbatim` labels an agent-synthesized `because` in p018-R9, p013-R7 and p021-R8-v2; p006-R3 prescribes a grep that no episode attests; p012-R7's `because` quotes a composite phrasing that appears verbatim in no turn; p011-R11's second `because` clause lies outside the verified window; and p014-R5 rests entirely on agent self-narration with no author turn in the window — it codifies behavior the agent performed correctly rather than a correction the author made.

1	# Goals and history — what BookMinder is for
2	
3	## Destination and core question
4	
5	- **B-01 — Destination.** An MCP tool for discussing books with Claude: the author reads on his iPhone and wants to talk with an LLM about the book he is reading, its last chapter, and the highlights made since the last conversation. CLI first, deliberately — the author knows CLI design and TDD/BDD cold, while MCP was unfamiliar territory; the CLI is the walking skeleton of the broader vision.
6	- **B-02 — Core question.** Can an LLM be a good pair programmer? The author had no colleagues to pair with; this project is the experiment. The method is the point: executable specifications nail verifiable invariants, and the art is slicing the problem and designing specs with minimal coupling to implementation — London school, GOOS lineage. The root principle everything else derives from: the spec's job is nailing requirements in a falsifiable way. Executable specification, GOOS layers, enforced layer separation, and delegation contracts all follow from falsifiability — a hierarchy, not parallel motivations.
7	- **B-03 — Why Apple Books as testbed.** Deliberately chosen because the Apple Books database schema is undocumented and evolves with each macOS release. That makes the project a test of long-term software evolution and maintenance — the opposite of one-shotting problems the model already knows from pretraining.
8	- **B-04 — Book-grounding motivation (product feeds process).** Pretrained simulacra of TDD/BDD experts proved shallow caricatures — skewed, non-actionable summaries of real positions. A core BookMinder motivation is giving the model access to full books as consultation material, so actionable principles can be extracted from primary sources that did not survive pretraining summarization. The failure-mode name for the thing this defeats: simulacra-shallowness.
9	- **B-05 — The project is a vehicle and a benchmark.** The real object of study is whether an AI coding agent can hold a strict ATDD process as a pair programmer; process artifacts are therefore deliverables, not cruft. The durable artifact chain is story cards expanded into acceptance tests, with working code as the output an agentic system must derive from them — the author (a Product Owner by day job, working in Jeff Patton's User Story Mapping tradition) has long intended the project to double as a benchmark of agentic coding systems.
10	
11	## History
12	
13	- **B-06 — BookMind, the predecessor.** BookMind implemented most of the original vision — EPUB parsing, highlight extraction, markdown export, a working CLI, 40 passing tests. It was not a failure. The fork to BookMinder was motivated by process, cost, and code quality: the agent took too much unrequested initiative and produced a sprawling codebase at high cost. Never describe BookMind as broken software, and never score BookMinder against BookMind on size, coverage, or feature count — BookMinder is a walking skeleton by explicit request, so the comparison measures the choice, not the outcome. `ORIGINAL_VISION.md` is a copy of BookMind's first README (verify with `git show 64dc71b:README.md` in the BookMind repo context), not a BookMinder-specific document.
14	- **B-07 — Scope discipline is the founding constraint.** BookMinder exists specifically to stop the agent from running ahead with its own creative ideas. The scope is the GOOS walking skeleton plus whatever the story cards ask for; add no capability the author has not asked for. CLAUDE.md is the instrument of that constraint.
15	- **B-08 — Apple-only by design.** Apple Books is the product's entire subject. Never propose, justify, or advertise a change on cross-platform grounds; CI pins macOS.
16	- **B-09 — Timeline in brief.** Summer 2025: intense development — a gold-standard ATDD era, then a process lapse after commit 6f786cc (features landed without proper ATDD; the repair backlog for this still stands) — ending in the author's burnout from holding process discipline for models that knew the process but could not perform it (knowing vs performing is the key distinction). ~1 year dormant. 2026-08: reevaluation sessions on cloud infrastructure — no new feature code; the 2025 session diary was mined into a rules corpus, the spec tree was restored wholesale to its pre-reorg concern-based form, commit-after-RED was restored to CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md became symlinks to CLAUDE.md, and this skill was compiled.
17	- **B-10 — The stickiness law.** Corrections shipped as automation (hooks, validators, CI) stick; shipped as prose they only partly stick. The author rates Claude Code hooks the most valuable CC innovation for exactly this reason: enforcement via automation, not prose. When a rule keeps being violated, the durable fix is machinery, and the open experiment question is how much harness enforcement discipline requires once skills are in place.
18

1	# Repo geography, backlog, and fixture architecture
2	
3	## Orientation
4	
5	- **B-20 — Cheapest grounding.** The production package is tiny (~290 lines: `bookminder/cli.py` + `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`) — read it whole before any task; it is cheaper than guessing. The behavior spec of the whole system is `pytest --spec`. Feature entry chain: `bookminder/cli.py` → `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`; everything else is docs, fixtures, or process. Never run unfiltered `find .` or repo-wide line counts — exclude caches, any vendored venv, and `claude-dev-log-diary/` from every listing or metric.
6	- **B-21 — Land mines.** `claude-dev-log-diary/` (~12M of hand-curated session transcripts) is permission-gated: never read, grep, commit, or surface it — including indirectly via `git diff`/`git show`/`git log -p` — without explicit user consent, and a grant is scoped to the exact excerpt and manner named (targeted range reads in the foreground; never whole-file reads, never background-subagent greps). One day-file may contain several sessions (`^claude` marks each start) and only the session-end cost figure is valid. `docs/ui/apple/` holds ~2.5M of binary screenshots — reference by path, never Read. `specs/apple_books/fixtures/All_Books*.swift` (~240K each) are grep-only and deliberately untracked pending curation — do not gitignore them and never stage them. Fixture `.sqlite` files are binary — query with `sqlite3`, never Read. The `./xs` symlink resolves into the forbidden diary directory: execute it as the documented tool, do not read it as a file. Zero-byte fixture files (`401429854.epub`, corrupted_db_user's plist+sqlite) are intentional — that is the fixture's point, not damage to repair.
7	- **B-22 — Spec tree layout.** Specs are concern-based at HEAD: `specs/cli_spec.py`, `specs/cli_formatting_spec.py`, `specs/apple_books/library_spec.py`, `specs/apple_books/library_integration_spec.py`, with fixtures co-located under `specs/apple_books/fixtures/`. A 2025 four-layer reorg (`unit/integration/acceptance/e2e`) was reverted wholesale in 2026-08 by checkpoint restore; those directories may linger as untracked `__pycache__` residue only — they are not tracked structure (confirm with `git ls-files specs/`). Coverage caveat: `specs/cli_spec.py` drives the CLI via `subprocess` (`sys.executable -m bookminder`, cli_spec.py:19-38), and pytest-cov does not follow child processes — never read a coverage gap in subprocess-exercised code as evidence it is untested.
8	
9	## Session-transcript preservation
10	
11	- **B-32 — Native transcript backup (cloud/ephemeral containers only).** `claude-dev-log-diary/jsonl/` preserves full session transcripts in the agentic system's native format — the machine-readable source the day-files only shadow; layout and copy commands live in its README. When working in an ephemeral container (Claude Code cloud infra), the container's transcript dies with it, so snapshot the session's `.jsonl` file + directory from the harness project store (`/root/.claude/projects/<project>/`) into `jsonl/cloud-<year>/` and commit: (1) always toward session end, when the final branch push is being prepared; (2) incrementally at natural stable points — after a major phase of work lands, or when resuming after a long pause (the pause's tail is then on disk). Copies are append-only extensions, so re-snapshotting is always safe; batch the snapshot into an adjacent commit rather than making high-frequency snapshot-only commits. A transcript cannot contain its own final minutes — the true tail of a session is captured by the next session's first snapshot. Local (non-ephemeral) sessions are exempt: the harness store persists there, and the author owns backup timing.
12	
13	## Backlog and stories
14	
15	- **B-23 — Backlog practice.** Stories are YAML cards under `stories/` in story-map columns: `discover` covers listing, filtering, admin access, and error handling; `access` is controlling the Apple Books app; `review` is highlights and notes; `export` is text extraction. Every card carries a mandatory `status` from the vocabulary CLAUDE.md `<backlog_management>` defines — status only, no priority/assignee metadata (YAGNI). TODO.md's Discover Column is a bare list of story paths in implementation order: the order is the plan, so take the next story in order rather than offering a menu, and keep the list free of emoji, numbering, and per-item rationale. Completed Features is an immutable record of the journey — never reorder or remove entries; annotate a reopened story in place (`[REOPENED: ...]`); refactorings are not listed there (user-visible stories only); a doc deletion gets a one-line breadcrumb with its commit hash. Parked backlog items must carry enough of the HOW (mechanism, trigger, expected behavior) that a fresh session can execute them without asking. Declared statuses can lie — verify against implementation and `git log` before acting on them (see current-state page).
16	
17	## Settled design decisions in the code
18	
19	- **B-24 — CLI shape.** `main` is a Click group; `list` is a subgroup declared `@main.group(name="list")` on a function named `list_cmd` — never name the function `list`, which shadows the builtin and breaks `list[Book]` annotations at import time (fix name collisions at the source, not with deprecated typing aliases). Subcommands `recent` and `all` share options via the `with_common_list_options` decorator (Click does not inherit group options). Filter vocabulary: one repeatable `--filter` option whose values are attribute names with `!` negation (`cloud`, `!cloud`, `sample`, `!sample`) — `!` and not `-` because Click parses a leading `-` as an option; filters are orthogonal to list commands (nothing in Apple Books' UI makes them command-specific). `list recent` deliberately replicates Apple's Continue section so that an agent consuming the future MCP surface and the human looking at the app share one frame of reference. `--user` is simultaneously a real admin feature (examine another user's books) and the test seam — the admin use case is what licenses it in production. The CLI owns no domain knowledge: it passes the raw `--user` string and filter through to the library and delegates path resolution and querying there.
20	- **B-25 — The Book type.** One `Book` TypedDict with `NotRequired` optional fields; never a parallel type for a variant that adds a field. 23	
24	- **B-26 — Synthetic $HOME personas and the front-door seam.** Integration fixtures are synthetic home-directory trees under `specs/apple_books/fixtures/users/<persona>/` replicating Apple's container layout path-for-path. Each persona encodes a container state observed on a real machine: `test_reader` (full library), `fresh_books_user` (all containers, empty plist, empty-schema sqlite), `legacy_books_user` (containers but no BKLibrary directory), `never_opened_user` (only the OS-created `com.apple.iBooksX` container — no BKAgentService, no plist, no sqlite), `corrupted_db_user` (zero-byte plist and sqlite; note a corruption scenario needs the full container present or the plist check fires before the sqlite error). The seam is the front door: `--user` with an absolute path is used verbatim as the home directory, a bare name resolves to `/Users/<name>`, `None` to `Path.home()` — exactly three cases, specced in `library._get_user_path`, no falsy-string case. Specs must pass absolute fixture paths (a relative path is treated as a username and silently rewritten). """Print corpus fragment truncated at the next top-level key, and its transcript windows."""
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, ".coordination/tools")
import rule  # noqa: E402

TOPKEY = re.compile(r"^[a-z_]+:")


def main(argv):
    ctx = 55
    ids = []
    it = iter(argv)
    for a in it:
        if a == "-c":
            ctx = int(next(it))
        else:
            ids.append(a)
    frags = rule.find_fragments(set(ids))
    for i in ids:
        if i not in frags:
            print(f"# NOT FOUND: {i}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        f, start, lines = frags[i]
        out = []
        for ln in lines:
            if TOPKEY.match(ln):
                break
            out.append(ln)
        text = "\n".join(out)
        print(f"# ===== {i} @ {f}:L{start + 1}")
        print(text)
        print()
        rule.print_transcript_windows(text, ctx)


main(sys.argv[1:])

## Roll-up — B-05

B-05 currently reads: *The real object of study is whether an AI coding agent can hold a strict ATDD process as a pair programmer; process artifacts are therefore deliverables, not cruft.* Verified as far as it goes — but every one of its sources is a turn where the author qualifies the claim in the same breath. At day-009:L8038-L8041 the benchmark idea and "It might be just turn out ot be just a big  baggage of AI slop in the end" are one sentence apart; at day-018:L5021 he affirms the vehicle framing and at L5056 calls most of `docs/` slop. Read without the qualifier, B-05 is a licence for exactly the artifact inflation the author spent day-018 deleting (12 files, 2,699 lines, commit eea59e3).

Proposed: keep the first clause, and bound the second to the artifacts the transcripts actually protect — *the deliverable process artifacts are the durable chain (story cards → acceptance tests → working code), the session diary, and the agent-instruction files; AI-written retrospective meta-analysis is not one of them (day-018:L5056-L5057, and see B-31)*. Cross-referencing B-31 costs one clause and closes the loop.

## Roll-up — B-20

## Roll-up — B-21

The diary-access clause is the best-evidenced rule in the range — four independent sessions, four different failure shapes — and only one phrase in it is unsupported. B-21 says a grant is scoped to "targeted range reads in the foreground; never whole-file reads, never background-subagent greps". The first and second are attested (day-014:L340-L341 grants one line range; day-014:L417-L419 punishes the whole-file read with "you just wasted 10% of your context on ingesting complete logs"). The third is attested for the *background subagent* only: at day-020:L56097 the author killed a `Task` doing a diary grep, and then watched four foreground `rg` sweeps over diary files without comment (L56101-L56116).

Proposed: keep the sentence, but make the tested boundary explicit rather than implying that any broad pattern search is forbidden — *…the grant is scoped to the excerpt and manner named: range reads over whole-file reads, and never from a background subagent, where the author cannot see or stop what is being read (day-020:L56097)*.
